goal: Across repeated supervisor starts the supervisor log directory's footprint stays at or under a configured ceiling by reclaiming the oldest logs while the most-recent log content survives.

relevant: packages/flywheel/src/flywheel/_autopilot_supervisor.py -- _open_log() (around lines 340-347) opens a NEW autopilot-supervisor-<ts>.log on every start with nothing reclaiming the old ones; bound the directory footprint here (rotation/cap/retention by age or count)
packages/flywheel/tests/test_autopilot_supervisor.py -- existing supervisor tests to keep green; the new bound must not break liveness/log-handle behavior
constraints: The bound reclaims the OLDEST supervisor logs while preserving at least the most-recent log content -- a 'rotation' that deletes/truncates everything (footprint zero, no logs survive) is a defect.
Footprint is held at or under a CONFIGURED ceiling (default-on); the magnitude is not load-bearing -- bounded + default-on is the requirement.
Keep this in the flywheel/supervisor layer; do not place log/disk logic in flywheel_core.task or flywheel_core.lifecycle (purity).
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not modify or weaken existing supervisor or autopilot tests; do not delete assertions.
Do not change the per-run telemetry JSONL retention (that is the bound-run-logs task).
Do not touch flywheel_core purity boundaries.
edge_cases: Fewer logs than the ceiling -- nothing is reclaimed (no over-eager deletion).
Exactly at the ceiling after a start -- the most-recent log must still be readable.
A reclaim that empties the directory must fail the test (recent content must survive).
